passage: I sit in the third row and saw Irfan debate whether uniforms should be compulsory. He opened with a survey the class had run, twenty-two out of thirty who said comfort mattered more. Then Zoya from the other team made the point that uniforms reduce pressure to compete with clothes, and Irfan paused. He said, "That's fair, I hadn't looked at it that way. But I'd still argue that a few casual days would keep the benefit." He didn't shout. His voice stayed level while his foot tapped. The other side actually nodded at him. Whether he changed his own mind, I can't say. But he sounded like he was listening, and he still held his ground. Abhinav.

qa.q: What did Irfan open his debate with?
qa.a: He opened with a survey the class had run.

qa.q: What might Irfan's tapping foot and level voice suggest?
qa.a: They suggest he felt some nervous energy but was managing it, since his voice stayed level. Abhinav can't tell whether Irfan changed his mind.

qa.q: What did Irfan do that strengthened his argument?
qa.a: He acknowledged Zoya's good point and then defended his own view with a specific proposal.

qa.q: How might the other team have felt about being acknowledged?
qa.a: They probably felt heard and respected, which is why they nodded at him.

grounding: A teen builds an argument with evidence, acknowledges a good point and defends a view, seen by an observer.

passage:
Monday. In the family debate about homework hours, Bhupen talked over everyone and called his sister Alka's point "stupid". She stopped speaking. He won the shouting and lost the room.
Wednesday. Bhupen asked his teacher for two studies on sleep and school. He wrote three points down and one thing Alka might say back.
Saturday. At dinner he said, "Alka, you were right that some homework builds habits. I'd like to argue that shorter tasks work as well, and here's a study." Alka leaned forward. "Okay, show me." They spent an hour going through it. Nobody won, but Papa said it was the best conversation they'd had in months.

qa.q: What did Bhupen call Alka's point on Monday?
Why did Bhupen prepare a point Alka might say back?
qa.a: He probably regretted calling her point stupid and losing the room on Monday, so he wanted to understand her view. It suggests he now cares about being fair as well as being right.

qa.q: What made the Saturday debate go better than Monday's?
qa.a: He used evidence, admitted a good point from Alka and stayed respectful instead of shouting.

qa.q: How might Alka have felt on Monday?
qa.a: She probably felt dismissed and silenced, which is why she stopped speaking.

grounding: A teen learns that debate skill includes evidence and acknowledging good points, and that ridicule and volume fail.
